name: BACH_0321_FSIM_resample3
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (91%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set and clean input, but the second model and all five neighbors disagree [F1][F5].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 91%, Normal 5%, InSitu 5%, Invasive 0% | Clear leader |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 1.0 | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 0/5 Benign; all Normal | Neighbors say Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↓ invasive · Scarce here; concept model links this to lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 4, 8) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; associated with non-invasive tissue · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 10) · ↓ invasive · Present; text-prompt only, caption check inconsistent · Validated
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (region 6) · context · Above typical; spot check 8/20 · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) spans 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. Case leans on mitoses (0/20, Unreliable) [F4].

## Could be wrong if
- Resampling degradation (severity 3) masks invasive features despite the high reliability score.
- Second model and all neighbors favor a different class, so Benign versus Normal is unresolved.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 4, 8** — confirm benign stroma and absent tumor-infiltrating stroma.
2. **Regions 1, 10** — verify glands are benign, not invasive tubules.
3. **Regions 3, 11** — lateral edge flagged tumor at margin [F7], conflicting with 0% invasive score.
